name: 02a_scoop_pickup
title: Scoop stretcher pickup
subtitle: Two G1s slide the halves of a scoop stretcher under a patient lying on the road, latch them, and lift on a count, keeping the stretcher level.

captions.text: The patient lies on the road shoulder. The scoop stretcher is split into two halves, one beside each side of the body.
Each G1 stoops low and takes its half by the outer rail. (Its ankles bend only 30 degrees, so it leans at the hips instead of squatting deep.)
Both blades slide under the patient at the same time, from opposite sides, so the body is not pushed sideways.
The blades meet under the spine. The G1s let go and stand.
A walks to the head end, B to the foot end.
They stoop at the ends, latch the halves together and take the end handles.
On the count: both ends rise at the same rate. If one end leads, the stretcher tilts and the patient slides.
Held level at hand height, ready to carry to the cot.
